facts: About $68\%$ of scores lie between $\mu-\sigma$ and $\mu+\sigma$.
About $95\%$ of scores lie between $\mu-2\sigma$ and $\mu+2\sigma$.
About $99.7\%$ of scores lie between $\mu-3\sigma$ and $\mu+3\sigma$.
The curve is symmetrical about the mean, so exactly $50\%$ of scores lie above $\mu$ and $50\%$ below.
Half of each central band sits on each side of the mean, so $34\%$ lies between $\mu$ and $\mu+\sigma$.
Each tail is half of what is left over, so beyond $\mu+2\sigma$ there is $(100\%-95\%)\div 2 = 2.5\%$.
A band between two boundaries is a difference, so between $\mu+\sigma$ and $\mu+2\sigma$ there is $47.5\%-34\% = 13.5\%$.
steps: Write each boundary as a number of standard deviations from the mean
Split the curve into the empirical-rule regions
Add the percentages inside the required region
